title: Absorption by a silent self-loop
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, let $q_a$ be a state, and suppose that in state $q_a$ the transition is always the action that keeps the input head fixed, makes no changes or movements on the work tapes, emits no output, and returns to $q_a$. Then, from any configuration on any Boolean input whose state is $q_a$, iterating the machine's step function any finite number of times leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number of work tapes
For every input symbol and work-tape reading, the transition in $q_a$ is the silent stationary self-loop
An initial configuration $c$ in state $q_a$ on input $x$
replaced:
If a control state's transition is the silent stationary self-loop, then from
any configuration in that state, a run of any length leaves the configuration
unchanged.
